question_text: Fill in: 'By the time the manager arrived, the staff ___ the reports.'

hint_ladder.title: Isipin ang Timeline
hint_ladder.text: Sa barangay hall, bago pumasok si Kap, tapos na reports. So dalawang nakaraan: nauna ang tapos, sumunod ang dating.

hint_ladder.title: Past Perfect = 'Past Before the Past'
hint_ladder.text: Kapag may mas naunang aksyon sa nakaraan, gamitin ang past perfect: 'had' + past participle (e.g., 'had finished').

hint_ladder.title: Hanapin ang Naunang Aksyon
hint_ladder.text: Ang blank ay tungkol sa pagtapos ng reports bago ang dating ni Kap. Kaya 'had already finished' ang tamang tense.

hint_ladder.title: I-eliminate ang Mali
hint_ladder.text: A: 'finish' present. B: 'finished' simple past. C: 'have finished' present perfect. D: 'had finished' past perfect—ito tamang 'past before the past'.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'finish' seems simple, but the timeline is past—present tense doesn't fit here.

B.text: You might have chosen B because 'finished' sounds past, but simple past can't show which action came first.

C.text: You might have chosen C because 'have finished' is familiar, but it's present perfect, not the earlier past needed.

D.text: Correct. 'Had already finished' uses past perfect to show the reports were done before the manager arrived.

next_time_rule: When you see 'by the time' + past event, the earlier action must be past perfect: 'had' + past participle. Think of it as the 'past before the past' signal.
deconstruct_text:
Isipin mo ang isang araw sa barangay hall. Bago dumating si Kap, tapos na ng staff lahat ng reports—expert mode na sila. So ang timeline: nauna ang tapos ng reports, sumunod ang dating ni Kap. Ibig sabihin, may naunang pangyayari sa nakaraan.

Kaya kailangan mo ng 'past perfect': 'had' + past participle. Dito, 'had already finished.' Kapag 'by the time' ang nakita mo sa past sentence, automatic dapat maisip mo 'had + V3.' Yung iba—'finish,' 'finished,' 'have finished'—kulang sila. Parang jeepney na walang ...
